episodes.title: First principles: What it takes to be a great product manager in the AI era | Sherif Mansour
episodes.description: Sherif Mansour is Head of AI and Product Craft at Atlassian (the company behind Jira and Confluence), where he has spent 17 years building and scaling some of the most successful enterprise products in history. He joined Atlassian as its first PM on Confluence, eventually becoming its first Distinguished PM, and now leads both the craft of product management across the company and Atlassian’s AI product strategy. We discuss: 1. Why a PM’s #1 job is to build a “shared brain” 2. The artist, the scientist, and the GM: three types of PM, and how to tell which one you are 3. Why PM roles are growing fastest in the AI era 4 Why Atlassian is hiring more juniors than ever 5. The most common mistake new PM managers make — Brought to you by: WorkOS —Make your app enterprise-ready, with SSO, SCIM, RB

episodes.title: Replay: How the Internet Happened | Chris Dixon & Brian McCullough (2018)
episodes.description: Why do technologies that look like bad ideas in one era become enormous companies in the next? Originally recorded in 2018, Brian McCullough and Chris Dixon trace the companies, failures, and accidents that built the modern internet. They revisit the battle between the open web and more centralized visions of the “information superhighway,” why eBay helped establish trust between strangers online, what Napster understood about digital media, and how Google found a business model for search. They also look at the dot-com crash and the ideas that arrived before the technology was ready, from cloud storage to grocery delivery, asking what those cycles can teach founders about spotting the next wave. episodes.title: Growth Comes From Outside Your Comfort Zone: Why Founders Are Leaving Home to Learn - E750
episodes.description: Should founders leave home to build? In this compilation, Jeremy Au, Shiyan Koh, Adriel Yong and Chalinda Abeykoon argue that the better question is how often to go, and what to bring back. Shiyan, Managing Partner at Hustle Fund, tells founders outside the Bay Area to spend time in San Francisco every quarter or so, without necessarily moving there. Adriel, co-founder and COO of Clouted, argues that Singapore works so well it dulls the problem-solving instinct founders need, and that every student should spend six months to a year abroad. Chalinda, Managing Partner at nVentures, grew up in Colombo during Sri Lanka’s civil war, when leaving was the plan for almost everyone, and now runs a fund that backs Sri Lankan founders.
